reader.requirement: At --std 85 every rule written for index-name-1, identifier-1 (SET format 1) and index-name-3 (format 2) must hold for each receiver of a SET receiver list, not just the first: each identifier-1 is screened by SR2 and by the format-1 operand table (GR3b/GR3c, GR5), each index-name-3 must be an index-name and is augmented (GR4), the sender value is the one at the start of the statement and each receiver's subscripts are evaluated just before its store (GR3d).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry set-arithmetic-expression-2002: at 85 the format 1/2 sender must be a 1985 operand (positive integer-1, signed integer-2, integer item, index-name, index data item); asked once per statement for the shared sender, not per receiver
diagnostic wording only (cites §1985:VI.6.23.2 and the 1985 brace/rule); format selection reads operand kinds, not the edition

reader.edition-search: grep -n -i 'DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior|Edition.Year|Edition.Edition' over SetBinder.cs, SetFormatSelection.cs, SetEmitter.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs and CobolIndex.cs (SetEmitter, ReceiverBracketEmitter and CobolIndex: none); the per-receiver loop in BindSetTo / BindSetUpDown has no edition term
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the recursion rule itself (every receiver screened the same way at 85 and 2023); the shared sender differs: SET IX JX TO 0 is refused at 85 (1985 integer-1 positive) and accepted at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover receiver identification at store and index overflow on one receiver; refusal of a second/later receiver by SR2/GR3, format-2 recursion over two index-names, and the sender-as-at-beginning rule with a sender subscripted by an earlier receiver are not exercised by them

probes.printed: COBOL2326 on the SECOND receiver of: SET IX N1 TO 2 (SR4/GR3c), SET IX NX TO JX (PIC XX, SR1/SR2), SET IX ID1 TO 2 (SR3/GR3b), SET JX NF TO IX (9V9 not integer); SET N1 ID1 TO ID1; COBOL2112 on SET IX N1 UP BY 1 (N1 not an index-name); COBOL0900 on SET IX JX TO 0 at 85 only
probes.expected: each refused for the offending recursion

SET IX JX TO 3 sets both (different tables); UP BY 2 and DOWN BY 1 augment each index-name-3; SET N1 N2 TO JX sets both; SET K NN (K) TO JX stores K=6 then NN(6)=6 (GR3d subscripting just before store); SET KX JX TO IDT (KX) gives JX the value IDT(2)=7 as at the beginning, not IDT(7)=3

probes.printed: line 21 SET IX JX TO 0: COBOL0900 at 85; no diagnostic at 2023

reader.notes: BindSetTo classifies the sender once and runs ScreenIndexAssignmentReceiver over every receiver in the list, and BindSetUpDown selects format 2 from the whole receiving list, so no receiver position escapes a rule. At run time the sender is evaluated once before the stores and each receiver is identified at its own store.
reader.at-2023: identical per-receiver refusals and run output; only the 1985 zero integer-1 refusal is absent
